paper_title: A Cross-Scenario Survey and Analysis of Self-Evolving Multimodal Agents

sections.title: Abstract
sections.content: Recent work shows that multimodal agents increasingly self-improve without recurring human annotation. However, each self-improvement mechanism is designed and evaluated within a single scenario, leaving its preconditions unverified under cross-scenario transfer. This survey investigates the structural source of asymmetric mechanism transfer across four scenarios: multimodal reasoning, multimodal generation, GUI and Web navigation, and embodied manipulation. We first formalize the self-evolving multimodal agent by four criteria and a differentia of self-reference, and adopt the three-stage self-evolving loop of experience generation, feedback acquisition, and update consolidation as our analytical framework to position the scenarios along ceilings on rollout count and feedback fidelity. Comparing self-evolving with fixed loops within each scenario separates the limitations that the scenario imposes from those inherent in the self-evolving design. We then recast each mechanism as a trade-off that raises a scarce factor by presupposing a task-structural resource, such as output equivalence or checkable outcomes, and judge it portable, conditional, blocked, or redundant across scenarios. We attribute the asymmetry to divergent combinations of scarce factors and resources across opposite transfer directions, and identify the matched-budget measurements that could overturn these still untested verdicts.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content: Recent advances in multimodal foundation models have fueled an explosive proliferation of multimodal agents [1, 2, 3, 4], spawning flourishing spectrum of self-evolution techniques across multimodal reasoning [5, 6, 7, 8], multimodal generation [9, 10, 11, 12, 13], GUI and Web navigation [14, 15, 16, 17], and embodied manipulation [18, 19, 20, 21]. Despite strong scenario-specific gains, existing selfevolving methods are designed and evaluated within single scenarios, and their mechanisms do not transfer equally well in both directions of scenario pair. For example, majority voting derives label-free rewards for reasoning tasks from consistency across sampled answers [5, 22, 23], yet finds no counterpart in embodied manipulation, where action trajectories admit no equivalence check and physical rollouts incur steep execution and reset costs. Conversely, world models circumvent expensive environmental interactions via imagined rollouts [24, 25], but raise factor that is not scarce in reasoning, where sampling directly from the policy costs little. Beneath this directional breakdown in mechanism transferability, which suggests cross-scenario asymmetry, also lies shared self-evolving loop across diverse tasks. Specifically, across all four scenarios, self-evolving agents share the same cycle, i.e., generating exploratory experience, acquiring evaluative feedback, and consolidating persistent updates. This survey investigates the structural source of cross-scenario asymmetry by characterizing this shared loop and explaining why the two directions of scenario pair meet different obstacles to transfer. However, as summarized in Table 1, existing work leaves this cross-scenario asymmetry unaddressed. Primary studies benchmark exclusively within specific scenarios [20, 40], while prior surveys either overlook the self-evolving loop as an analytical object [1, 2, 3, 41, 42] or formalize it as scenarioagnostic [28, 31, 33]. Even the closest related work [29] attributes verifiable feedback and retraining costs to domainlevel paradigms, not to specific mechanisms. To fill this gap, we first formalize the surveyed object through genus and differentia. The genus comprises autonomous learning loops satisfying four criteria: (i) autonomy, where the agent operates without human intervention across goals, actions, feedback, and updates post-initialization; (ii) freshness, where experience is generated under the current policy; (iii) durability, where updates persist beyond the episode boundary; and (iv) recurrence, where the loop iterates across cycles. The differentia, self-reference, requires the agent to realize at least one component of its own loop: the goal sampler, the feedback function, or the evolution operator. Loops in the genus lacking self-reference, termed fixed loops, serve as controls across all scenarios to disentangle scenario-imposed constraints from the intrinsic effects of self-evolution. We formalize each stages bottleneck through two governing factors: (i) rollout count and information gain, (ii) feedback fidelity and credit localization, and (iii) retention and generalization. Each scenario imposes ceilings on the rollouts affordable per cycle ( K) and the feedback fidelity attainable by admissible evaluators ( ), which span two-dimensional positioning matrix. In this matrix, multimodal reasoning is situated where both ceilings are high, multimodal generation where is low, GUI and Web navigation where is low, and embodied manipulation where both are low, with simulation raising both ceilings. Comparing self-evolving and fixed loops within each cell further separates the limits imposed by scenario ceilings from those incurred by self-evolving design, e.g., replacing answer keys with sampled consensus in reasoning [5, 22]. The matrix thus identifies which ceilings bind in each scenario, but alone cannot determine whether given mechanism is portable. Building on this matrix, we formulate each self-evolving mechanism as trade-off, in which the agent raises scarce factor by replacing fixed component with its own records, proposals, judgments, or memory writes, at the price of presupposing task-structural resource, such as output equivalence or checkable outcomes. In target scenario, mechanism is thus portable if the target holds this resource, conditional if it holds the resource only for sub-family or after adaptation, blocked if the outcome to be judged is unobservable, and redundant if the raised factor is not scarce. We attribute the cross-scenario asymmetry structurally to the different combinations of scarce factors and resources that the two directions of scenario pair encounter: e.g., voting finds no output equivalence in manipulation, whereas world models raise factor that is not scarce in reasoning. These verdicts, inferred from single-scenario evidence and not yet tested, define testable preconditions, not empirical guarantees. gain over budget-matched ablation without self-evolution would overturn any verdict that predicts no benefit from an unadapted transfer, which turns these predictions into concrete measurement agenda. This paper makes four contributions, the first two to the survey and the last two to the analysis. condition-based definition and paradigm demarcation. We operationalize autonomy and the differentia through provenance matrix that records which party realizes each loop component, and apply the definition to sixteen neighboring paradigms, of which five fall outside the genus, two never satisfy the differentia, five are divided by it, and four are self-evolving by definition. stage-resolved review and positioning matrix. We review each scenario through the three-stage self-evolving loop, place the four scenarios in the positioning matrix, contrast self-evolving with fixed loops in each cell, and trace five degradation modes along the cross-cycle paths through which they propagate. Directed portability across scenario pairs. We recast the mechanisms of all four scenarios as trade-offs and assign each portability verdict for every target scenario, yielding structural account of the cross-scenario asymmetry. falsifiable measurement agenda. We review the evaluation of task-solving capability, self-evolving capability, and judges, and identify the measurements whose absence leaves untestable three claims, i.e., that gain stems from self-evolution, that scenario occupies its assigned position, and that the verdicts hold. The remainder of this paper is organized as follows. Sec. 2 defines the surveyed object, and Sec. 3 develops the threestage loop and the positioning matrix. Secs. 4 to 7 review the four scenarios, and Sec. 8 derives the portability verdicts. Finally, Sec. 9 treats evaluation, and Secs. 10 and 11 discuss open challenges and conclude.

sections.title: 2 Preliminaries
sections.content: Conceptually, multimodal agent is goal-directed decisionmaking system that interacts with an external environment through closed perception-cognition-action loop over heterogeneous observation and scenario-specific action spaces [43]. We restrict the scope to agents whose cognitive core is large (multimodal) foundation model [44, 45, 46, 47, 48, 49, 50, 51] extended via interface [52, 53, 54], memory [55], and tools [56, 57, 58, 59], excluding architectures lacking such core, such as world-model planners and taskspecific visuomotor policies. Since the environment supplies perceptions, accepts actions, and specifies goals, we adopt multimodal agent-environment interaction as our formal scaffold. To systematically diagnose the cross-scenario asymmetry, we unfold this loop across two temporal scales: micro-scale capturing step-by-step behaviors within single episode, and macro-scale tracking the cycle-by-cycle evolution of the agents own components over long-term experiences. The resulting dual-scale dynamics are formalized under goalconditioned partially observable Markov decision processes (POMDPs) [60, 61]. On this scaffold, we define the surveyed object across four levels, from the static agent and environment through the learning loop and the autonomous learning loop to the self-evolving loop.

sections.title: 2.4 Demarcation from Established Paradigms
sections.content: The term self-evolving shares vocabulary with several established paradigms, and recent surveys draw its boundary at different points [28, 31, 34, 113, 114]. Table 2 compares adjacent paradigms; contested boundaries hinge on the entry. In the goal-sampler row, discarding tied groups within batch adds no entry [62], whereas allocating subsequent rollouts by task success qualifies [115]. In the evolutionoperator row, the test is who writes the update: separate fixed model (e.g., GPT-4o guiding GPT-3.5-Turbo in TextGrad) keeps the loop fixed [102, 104], whereas the acting model itself, as with ExpeLs insights [66] or STaRs rationales for failed instances [92], establishes self-evolution. Reflexion [116], where the acting model preserves self-reflections across episodic trials, qualifies as self-evolving, although its reflections, written for one task, improve no other task. Antiforgetting mechanisms of continual learning map onto the evolution operator fζ , whereas classical curriculum samplers such as POET [117], PLR and other regret-based environment designers [118, 119, 120], goal-proposing teachers [121, 122], and expert-iteration and AlphaZero self-play [123, 124] remain outside our foundation-model scope.

sections.title: 3.1 Loop Decomposition
sections.content: As shown in Figure 2, we factor each cycle into three scenarioinvariant stages, each organized around one meta-operator (σω, Vν , fζ ). This decomposition applies across the entire genus of autonomous learning loops and treats auxiliary operations, such as credit assignment or data filtering, as refinements within stage, not as additional stages. Stage 1 Experience Generation (EG): the goal sampler σω , and the current agent Ak draws the goal batch gk , producing rolls out in Pg for each goal gk the trajectory batch Dk. Through the quantity and informativeness of Dk, the only trajectories FA and UC act on, EG bounds how fast and how broadly the loop can evolve (speed and breadth). Stage 2 Feedback Acquisition (FA): the feedback function Vν maps Dk, together with the agent history A0:k when Vν reads the agent, to scores, preferences, or critiques sourced from the environment, the bootstrap, or the agent itself. FA is the loops only source of information about the idealized task reward (the R-aligned direction). Stage 3 Update Consolidation (UC): the evolution operator fζ computes an update from (Ak, Hk, Dk, Vν(Dk)) and writes it into at least one persistent component of Ak, producing the next-cycle agent Ak+1. UC determines whether an update persists across later cycles and generalizes beyond the goals that produced it (retention and generalization). The six factors originate at the two scales of Figure 1. The per-episode cost c(τ ) governing and action localization Lν arise within the micro-scale interaction loop, whereas information gain, evaluator fidelity Fν , and consolidation factors (Sζ , Gζ ) emerge from the macro-scale learning loop, the positioning matrix thereby pairing micro-scale axis with macro-scale one.

Sampling schemes escalate in intervention from random sampling [65] through curriculum mining over past failures [17, 135] and active task selection [136, 137] to environment synthesis [63, 138, 139, 140, 141]. Single-pass generation and tool-augmented reasoning yield single-action episodes, whereas digital and embodied environments expose multi-step state transitions whose informativeness depends on platform dynamics, reset conditions, and observability. Where closed-form success condition or discrete answer space exists, deterministic instruments such as answers computed by task generation [64, 146], unit tests [147, 148], and physicalconstraint rewards [18, 145, 149] sustain high Fν at modest cost. Lacking both, evaluators rely on self-rewards [9, 10, 150, 151], reward models [135, 144, 152, 153, 154, 155, 156], or VLM judges [14, 18, 157, 158], and gaming resistance binds [9, 159]. Quadrant Assignment. We place each scenario in quadrant of Figure 3 by the height of its two ceilings, calling ceiling binding when it is low. Multimodal reasoning faces neither low ceiling, multimodal generation low on openended prompts, GUI/Web navigation low under latencybound episodes in sandboxed environments whose end states per-task scripts inspect, and embodied manipulation both in physical deployment, its target. Three displacements, drawn dashed in the matrix, qualify this placement: (i) most embodied loops learn in simulation, where success predicates raise and group sampling eases K, shifting the operating point toward the navigation cell; (ii) generation contains verifiable sub-families such as OCR-scored prompts [195, 196, 197, 198, 199] and program-rendered charts [191], raising toward the reasoning cell; and (iii) navigation on live websites or free-form goals lacks state scripts and falls to screenshot judges [101, 200, 201], lowering toward the manipulation cell. The four scenarios thus occupy four quadrants, consistent with the bottom rows of Tables 3 and 4, and the two off-diagonal cells, cheap but gameable generation and costly but verifiable navigation, are combinations that single difficulty ordering would merge. In the absence of any study that estimates either ceiling under one definition in more than one scenario, the placement remains inferred from reported operating points. Backbone Prior as Confound. The backbone A0 confounds this placement by bounding what loop can reach independently of task structure. In text-only models, selfverification sharpens model toward outputs it already ranks highly [202], reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards narrows the problems solved at large sampling budgets [203], and gains from spurious rewards vary with the model family [204]. Backbones also differ across scenarios, from vision-language models pretrained on large questionanswering corpora in reasoning to action policies with far less motor pretraining in manipulation. Part of the contrast that the matrix attributes to and may thus reflect backbone coverage, factor that stays entangled with task structure. Feasibility Filter. sections.content: Beyond the matrixs within-cycle bounds, the recurrence of Eq. (5) couples successive cycles. It feeds two cycle-k outputs into Stage 1 of cycle k+1, the updated agent Ak+1 that induces the next rollout policy and the extended history Hk+1 that conditions the next goal draw, each defining directed edge across the cycle boundary. Environmental drift, which Definition 4 holds fixed but live websites exhibit [200, 205], enters as third path from outside the loop. These paths carry both self-reference and long-run degradation. Two Coupling Edges. The two edges differ in carrier and conditionality. The agent edge runs from Stage 3 of cycle to Stage 1 of cycle k+1, carrying the persisted update into Ak+1 and hence into the rollout distribution of Dk+1. Present in every autonomous learning loop, it supplies the closure on which C4 rests and extends to any further component that reads the current agent: to σω under trained proposer [5, 22], to Stage 2 under an evaluator sharing Φθ [6, 22], rendering (k) endogenous, and to Stage 3 under generative model ν that records lessons or skills [20, 162]. The goal edge runs from Stages 1 and 2 of cycle to Stage 1 of cycle k+1 through σω(k+1, Hk+1), carrying the cycle-k trajectories and their scores into the next goal draw. stationary or scheduled sampler, reading no cycle-specific signal, leaves this edge inert, whereas an adaptive sampler activates it and superimposes second feedback loop on the agent edge. Selfreference thus acts through the extensions of the agent edge and through the goal edge: fixed-loop method retains only the agent edge into Stage 1, and frozen snapshot satisfies self-reference without opening any of these paths. Five Degradation Modes. We interpret long-run degradation through these paths under mitigation-locality reading, in which the stage where degradation surfaces, the path that carries it, and the stage where it is best mitigated need not coincide, and Table 6 records all three for five modes. Compounding reward hacking and distribution shift travel along the agent edge as the in-support and extrapolation variants of Goodharts law [206], which rewardmodel overoptimization exhibits together [207], with shift also entering along the environment path [14, 200]. Forgetting and plasticity loss follow moving goal distribution carried by the environment path or the goal edge [192], and the two collapse modes contract the support of EG, curriculum collapse through the goal edge or the agent edge into σω [5, 131] and model collapse through the agent edge under any sampler [193]. The three loci diverge most for hacking and forgetting, which both surface at UC yet admit remedies upstream of the symptom, tighter Fν at FA [9] and replay in EG. Long-cycle drift compounds the first three modes within one task family and forms no sixth mode. The agentedge extension into UC, absent from the table, surfaces through erroneous writes, within single pass in MobileAgent-E [162] and across later rollouts in SEAR [20]. With existing loops running only few rounds, these mechanisms are inferred from within-run and fixed-loop evidence, and the reading stops at the cycle boundary. Scenario Exposure. The scenarios engage these paths unequally. In reasoning, learned proposer extends the agent edge into σω and pass-rate curricula open the goal edge [208, 209], both inviting curriculum collapse. Reasoning and generation both extend the agent edge into FA through self-referential verifiers, yet the outcome follows : under reasonings high ceiling, (k) drifts below , whereas ν under generations low ceiling, compounding hacking sets in unless frozen judge cuts that extension. In navigation and manipulation, task or environment changes drive shift and forgetting along the environment path and agent edge, and costly rollouts limit the EG resampling that counters them. Coupling thus extends the asymmetry across cycles.

Weight-updating loops mostly pose their own questions or train on unlabeled ones, letting the agents outputs supply most answers and tying the evaluator to the model it trains, which makes the realized fidelity (k) , not , the binding factor. sections.title: 4.1 EG Bound by Informative Goals
sections.content: Experience generation in multimodal reasoning draws goals that pair visual input (an image, video clip, or frames of 3D scene) with question whose short final answer admits an equivalence check. The task families center on visual question answering over mathematical, chart, and diagram inputs [240, 241, 242], extending to pairwise quality judgments [211], temporally grounded video questions [127, 160], metric spatial questions over 3D scenes [235], and physical dynamics in videos [209, 226, 239]. These goals come from dataset, fixed generator, or generative roles of the agent, and in weight-updating loops the solver typically answers each goal in Kk independent decoding passes, occasionally with tool calls, yielding Dk that groups answers to the same question, whereas training-free loops run the frozen VLM on each goal with its current skills, tools, or notes. Table 7 summarizes the self-evolving methods that satisfy the conditions of Sec. 2.3. Quantity and Quality Constraints. Experience generation is bound by quality at saturation  (Table 3)  , the task structure leaving quantity slack. rollout is single decoding pass over static input, an episode with = 1 except where tool calls precede the answer [216, 220, 224, 225, 228, 232], and leaves no side effect to revert, keeping both interaction cost and recoverability from lowering K. Information gain, in contrast, arises in single-answer episodes only from goals whose pass rate under the current solver lies strictly between zero and one. dataset or fixed generator bounds the supply of such goals by how many lie near the edge of the current agents competence, number that depends on the backbones pretraining and, by the mechanism that stalls self-play [131], shrinks as the agent masters these goals. Self-Posed Goals. Larger groups do not appear to substitute for informative goals under self-consistency rewards, which lose contrast as groups grow, and loops raise the information gain instead by letting the agent pose its goals or by reweighting goals by pass rate, at cost paid in feedback. Reported group sizes stay between four and ten rollouts per goal despite cheap decoding passes [6, 7, 8, 22, 126, 127, 215, 216, 218, 232, 234], and EvoLMM finds its selfconsistency reward best at four to six samples, reporting over-consensus collapse at twelve [22], consistent with the reward, not the cost, limiting Kk. The agent enters σω either as generative role within Φθ that synthesizes the question beside the solver, and in some loops the visual input, or through rule that reweights dataset or generator goals by the solvers pass rate, alone in SyncLoop [208] or on top of learned proposer [209, 237, 239]. Proposer-solver loops after R-Zero [243] reward goals of intermediate solver agreement through terms that vanish with pg(1 pg) [126, 234], adding diversity terms against narrowing of goals [5, 127]. These rewards are computed in FA yet reshape the goal distribution of EG. In VisPlay, trained Questioner lifts Qwen2.5-VL-3B from 30.61 to 44.16 after one round against 33.77 for an untrained Challenger [5], comparison that attributes about three quarters of the gain to learning the role. The gain is paid in feedback, where self-posed question lacks key unless program computes its answer, leaving the answer to the agents own outputs.

With localization free, every deficit of feedback acquisition is fidelity deficit, and self-derived rewards make that fidelity property of the model being trained. vote recovers the models belief and tracks only where answers admit an equivalence relation and the pretrained prior concentrates on the correct answer [80, 132], discrete answers supplying the first condition and the backbone, not the task structure, deciding the second. The evaluators further differ in whether they move with the policy: votes over current samples, parametersharing supervisors [126], and self-judging models [214] keep the agent edge into FA, judges frozen at the initial model cut it [212, 230], and the moving-average verifier of Trinity lags the policy by construction [231]. frozen evaluator still shares the prior of the policies descended from it, removing drift but not fixed bias, and reports under differing numbers of rounds leave the designs uncompared. sections.title: 4.3 UC Bound by Retention
sections.content: Update consolidation in multimodal reasoning persists the scored experience in two forms, weight updates and trainingfree writes  (Table 7)  . Weight-updating methods write Φθ with an update rule fixed before the loop, through grouprelative policy gradients, preference optimization, or finetuning, either once per round over two to nine reported rounds [5, 64, 160, 209, 214, 235, 238] or continuously within single training run. Training-free methods keep frozen VLM and let the agent write text or code into skill and tool libraries [146, 220, 223, 225, 227], memory cards or notes [219, 222, 226], or harnesses of tools, skills, and execution code [224, 233], over benchmark streams or, in VisualEvolve, up to sixteen rounds, whereas separate o4-mini abstracts the tool library of TVP [217]. MetaForge alone combines the two, registering validated tools that its policy forges during GRPO into persistent library [228]. Retention and Generalization Constraints. Update consolidation is bound by retention  (Table 5)  , inferred from nonmonotone curves, not measured loss, whereas generalization, though reported, is confounded with the backbone prior. No method measures retention on earlier-round goals, and the closest evidence, per-round scores on fixed benchmark suite, traces the increment Jk+1 Jk of Eq. (6) over the evaluation distribution, not the trained goals. These curves rise monotonically in Agent0-VL [216] but peak or dip midrun elsewhere [5, 8], while single benchmarks reverse more often, MM-Vet falling from 48.62 to 38.07 over three VisPlay iterations as the average rises [5]. Among weight-updating methods, only ISR-DPO and Marvo run beyond five rounds, the former gaining through its ninth iteration [214] and the latter degrading after about the fifth or sixth of eight [232]. Parametric writes generalize more freely, reaching any goal 16 that activates the updated weights and lifting standard benchmarks after training on synthesized questions [5, 7, 22]. These gains are consistent with elicitation of the backbone prior, most weight-updating methods resting on Qwen2.5VL or Qwen3-VL, the family whose text-only counterparts gain even under spurious rewards [204]. V-Zero offers partial control, reaching 51.9 against 50.8 for supervised GRPO on the same Qwen2.5-VL-7B backbone [7], and only an equal-budget non-evolving baseline would separate self-evolution from elicitation. Non-parametric writes act only when retrieved, and their transfer is tested directly, EvoSpatial evaluating libraries frozen after one benchmark on 18 others [220] and VideoEvoHarness moving an evolved harness to second backbone [233]. Reference-Gated Writes. Consolidation inherits its exposure from the first two stages, and the two forms of writing differ in how they guard against it. Where the evaluator moves with the policy or proposer supplies the goals, parametric write is scored and driven by quantities that change with the update itself, and the update rule accepts every scored step without fixed reference that could reveal later round erasing an earlier gain. Several training-free methods gate their writes against such reference, admitting skill or change only on validation or held-out gain [146, 233], promoting skill-tool pair only on strict gain over its training sample [225], rolling back note edits that do not raise batch accuracy [222], or selecting snapshots on fixed validation or development sets [223, 224], whereas TVP checks new tool only against the outputs of the programs it replaces [217]. guard on retention thus exists only where gated training-free writes keep fixed reference.

sections.title: 4.4 Limits and Preconditions
sections.content: Bottleneck Attribution. The binding bottlenecks of feedback and consolidation arise from self-reference, not from task structure. Both ceilings are slack for any learning loop, and fixed loop that trains against pre-collected keys, as M-STAR does [152], scores its rollouts at the fidelity of an exact match. The weight-updating branch gives up this reference to pose and answer its own questions, its answers coming from the agents own outputs, whose realized fidelity falls below , and its parametric writes lacking fixed reference against which later round could be checked. The training-free branch keeps the key or validation set and admits selfreference only through the update, shifting the cost to the writer, whose frozen backbone both diagnoses bottleneck and writes its remedy, its capability bounding both, limitation that Dynamo reports for itself [225]. Self-reference repays part of this cost in experience generation, where learned proposer relieves the saturation of fixed goal supplies and accounts for most of the first-round gain of VisPlay [5]. The few cross-round audits report declines confounded with rising question difficulty, and large question-answering prior in the backbones may account for part of the gains in both branches, disqualifying the least constrained cell as clean baseline for the other scenarios. This attribution rests on the stage evidence and on the provenance of each method in Table 7, not on controlled comparison with fixed loops. Cross-Cycle Degradation. Across cycles, self-reference exposes multimodal reasoning to degradations that fixed loop with keys avoids. On the goal side, learned proposers extend the agent edge into σω and pass-rate curricula open the goal edge [208, 209, 237, 239], both inviting curriculum collapse. On the feedback side, self-derived rewards extend the agent edge into FA, inviting compounding reward hacking, and training on self-labeled answers invites model collapse along the edge into the rollout policy. The extension of training-free writers into UC remains untested, and cross-round evidence reduces to the Vision-Zero plateau, where self-derived signal stops informing updates [218], and the late-round decline of Marvo [232], with per-round reversals of single benchmarks fitting hacking and forgetting alike. Presupposed Resources. The mechanisms of multimodal reasoning presuppose resources that its short, discrete answers supply. Majority votes and agreement-based proposer rewards presuppose answers that admit an equivalence relation [22, 126, 234], program-computed answers presuppose program that determines the answer at task generation [64], and reference-gated writes presuppose key or validation set held outside the writer [146, 225].

sections.title: 5 Self-Evolution in Multimodal Generation
sections.content: Multimodal generation occupies the quadrant of Figure 3 in which only the fidelity ceiling is low, an open-ended image or video having no reference output to be checked against outside sub-families such as object counts, rendered text, or program-drawn charts. Training against learned preference scorers fixed before the loop forms fixed loop that this ceiling already binds, such scorers being exploitable under optimization [129, 245]. Weight-updating loops mostly derive the verifier from the agent, leaving the ceiling unchanged but letting the verifiers bias move with the policy and exposing the loop to compounding reward hacking. Training-free loops mostly let frozen backbone judge its own outputs and write its memory or skills, sharing one bias between judge and writer. Reported loops run within one training run, over at most five rounds, or over one pass of task stream. 17 three to sixteen samples per prompt [9, 13, 128, 129, 245, 257]. Information gain, in contrast, runs out at the edge of what check can score, not at the edge of the agents competence as in multimodal reasoning. Fixed pools come from benchmark categories whose attributes detector, OCR, or VQA model scores, such as those of GenEval and T2I-CompBench [10, 11, 128, 129], and learning loop drives pass rates on such pool toward one, where pg(1 pg) approaches zero, as the fixed loop Flow-GRPO raises SD3.5-M from 0.63 to 0.95 on GenEval [195]. Open-ended prompts would still separate good outputs from poor ones under R, yet no check fixed before the loop scores them, leaving the loop unable to draw information from them. Loops drawing every round from one prompt distribution report diminishing gains by about the third round, consistent with this saturation [12, 248]. Checkable Goal Composition. larger group adds samples of prompt without extending the checkable pool, and loops raise E[IAk ] instead by letting the agent compose or reselect goals, at cost paid in fidelity once the goals leave what fixed check scores. Built-in checks keep composed goals within checkable sub-families, fixing answers at prompt construction in UniRL [128], decomposing each prompt into yes/no questions in SILMM [12], and restricting the specifications that RSI in UMMs plans from its own failures to charts that program execution verifies [191]. Goals beyond these sub-families fall to frozen external judges [258, 259, 260], whereas ASG poses understanding questions over unlabeled images, scored by the agreement of its own answers across framings at fidelity that moves with the policy [40], and reselection stays within the pool, InternalGap regenerating the prompts that yielded no accepted image [11]. Controlled returns are reported only for built-in checks and external judges, RSI in UMMs reaching 59.0% on charts after four rounds against 46.3% for longer training on its original data and leading fixed distribution of equally many verified charts in every round [191], and RSIgen gaining 4.7, 3.1, and 2.2 points over curricula compiled from frozen sources across its three attempts [260].

5.3 UC Bound by Retention
Update consolidation in multimodal generation persists the
scored experience in two forms, weight updates and training-
free writes (Table 8). Weight-updating methods write Φθ with
an update rule fixed before the loop, through group-relative
sections.content: policy gradients, preference optimization, fine-tuning, or self-distillation, either continuously within single training run or over two to five reported rounds [12, 191, 246, 247, 248, 249]. Training-free methods keep the generator and the agent frozen and let the agent write memory [165, 250, 253, 256, 265], skill, constraint-function, concept, or middleware libraries [103, 254, 255, 264], or routing records [258], over task stream or up to five rounds. ImageRSI alone combines the two, admitting experience to library while retraining its judge and not its generator [262]. Retention and Generalization Constraints. Update consolidation is bound by retention  (Table 5)  , documented within runs and in RSI in UMMs over at most four rounds, whereas generalization is mostly untested and not shown to fail. Only RSI in UMMs measures retention on earlier-round goals, exact category text on an earlier vocabulary falling from 72% to 60% once round replaces that vocabulary and recovering when later rounds keep half of the old specifications, while general understanding, which the chart goals do not exercise, erodes by 2.6 points on MMBench [191]. Within single runs, iteration robustness fails at the grain of optimizer steps, SOLACE degenerating into textureless images under prolonged optimization [9] and IRIS into meaningless images within hundreds of steps [129], and across rounds, perround scores cannot separate saturation from erosion, as in the slight slip of DreamLLM under SILMM on DPGBench [12]. Generalization is tested only where loop holds out evaluation goals [129, 253, 262], which MemoGen does not [265], and transfer is partial for both forms of writing, memory that SIDiffAgent builds on GenAI-Bench raising DrawBench from 0.860 to 0.873 against 0.901 for in-domain memory [165] and the parametric writes of RSI in UMMs gaining only from 11.0% to 11.9% on chart subset its authors judge too hard for open models [191]. Understanding-branch gains also remain entangled with the prior that judge and generator share in unified model. Self-Judged Writes. The exposure that consolidation faces comes from feedback acquisition, where the agent itself judges most writes, and the two forms of writing guard against it differently. Where the verifier depends on the policy, parametric write is scored by the policy itself or by judge that follows it, and the update rule admits every rewarded step, held back only by regularizers such as KL penalties [9, 10, 13, 40, 128, 129]. Training-free writes pass an admission test before they persist, yet the reviewer gating of ManimAgent [256] and the no-loss check of COMFYCLAW on three held-out prompts that the agent synthesizes [264] reuse the frozen model that judged the experience, protecting retention on that models scale but not against its bias. Only ImageRSI, through paired validation on separate calibration and holdout splits [262], and Drawing Middleware Evolution, through rollback against reference illustrations [255], test writes outside that model. Retention is thus protected only where training-free write is tested outside the model that judged it, condition that the keyor validation-gated writes of multimodal reasoning meet more often.

sections.title:
6 Self-Evolution in GUI and Web Naviga-
tion
sections.content: GUI and Web navigation occupies the quadrant of Figure 3 in which only the quantity ceiling is low, each rollout being multi-step episode that pays environment latency at every step, whereas the inspectable end state of an application or 20 web page keeps the attainable fidelity high in sandboxed environments, where per-task scripts read it. Much automated online learning here runs as fixed loops, whose tasks and verifiers come from external models or benchmark authors and never read the agents record [101, 130, 200, 268, 269, 270, 271, 272, 273, 274, 275, 276, 277]. Weight-updating loops allocate scarce rollouts by proposing goals or reweighting fixed task set by its success record, and buy step-level credit with verifiers refit on the agents trajectories, whose fidelity moves with the policy. Training-free loops keep the task set fixed and reuse each episode through memory or skills that frozen backbone writes and judges, sharing one bias between judge and writer. Reported loops span one training run, few rounds, or one pass over task stream, mostly evaluated on the task sets they train on.

sections.title: 6.1 EG Bound by Rollout Cost
sections.content: In GUI and Web navigation, experience generation draws goals that pair natural-language instruction with the initial state of an application, desktop, or website, and each rollout is an episode of screenshots, often with an accessibility tree, and actions such as taps, typing, and scrolls, ending in success, failure, or step limit. The task families span mobile apps in AitW, AndroidWorld, and AndroidLab [14, 17, 135], desktop software in OSWorld [16, 115, 278], and web navigation in WebArena and VisualWebArena sandboxes and on live WebVoyager and Online-Mind2Web sites [163, 201, 284]. These goals come from benchmark task set, task stream, or the agents own proposals, and weight-updating loops run episode groups per goal in parallel instances, whereas training-free loops run one or few episodes in sequence with frozen backbone. Table 9 summarizes the self-evolving methods that satisfy the conditions of Sec. 2.3. Quantity and Quality Constraints. Experience generation is bound by quantity at the episodes that parallel environment instances afford  (Table 3)  , an episode cost that the single passes of multimodal reasoning and generation do not incur. rollout spans up to 25 screen-action steps [130], each paying rendering and environment latency on top of policy inference, 2.5 to 4.0 seconds per step on the virtual machines of UITARS-2 [125], with DART-GUI reporting episodes that last tens of minutes [115]. Group sizes of eight to 64 rollouts per task [17, 101, 115, 130] are bought with parallel instances, up to 64 emulators in DigiRL [14], whereas training-free loops run each task once or few times in sequence [162, 163, 280, 281]. Quality decides what each scarce episode returns, and on long-horizon tasks the loss falls mostly on goals beyond the agents reach, where binary outcome gives pg(1 pg) 0, consistent with starting success rates of 11.3% on the professional software of SEAgent [16] and 18.1% on AndroidLab in UI-Genie [135]. Reuse, Reweighting, and Goal Generation. larger group costs environment instances, and loops raise E[IAk ] instead along three routes, reuse, reweighting, and goal generation, which the inspectable end state keeps verifiable. Under stationary sampling, reuse raises the return of later episodes by conditioning them on memory and skills that the agent writes [162, 163, 278, 279, 280, 281, 282, 283] or by training the agent on steps that value functions or reward models fit on its rollouts select and label [14, 144], both lifting unreachable 21 TABLE 9: Self-evolving methods for GUI and Web navigation. sections.title:
6.2 FA Bound by Localization
Each cycle hands feedback acquisition an episode of screens
and actions, which most loops score once at its end and loops
with learned step judges score per step (Table 9). Scores from
outside the agent (b) come from per-task scripts and rule-
based rewards written with the benchmark [17, 115], the fixed
evaluators of DigiRL and SEAgent [14, 16], and benchmark
success [280]. Scores from the agent (a) come from value
functions and reward models fit on its trajectories [14, 135,
144], the Judger role of the base model that SCALE fine-tunes
in its other roles [284], and the frozen backbone that acts and
sections.content: judges its own episode in training-free loops [162, 163, 201, 278, 279, 281]. Weight-updating methods turn scores into group-normalized advantages or rejection-sampled training targets [17, 115, 135, 144], whereas training-free methods turn them into success labels and diagnoses that gate memory and skill writes [163, 278, 281]. Fidelity and Localization Constraints. Feedback acquisition is bound by localization  (Table 4)  , the attainable fidelity being high wherever the goal fixes an end state, though signal sources reach that ceiling unevenly. Task completion resides in the final screen, application database, or file system, which per-task scripts and rule-based rewards inspect directly [17, 115], whereas model judges fall short, EvoSkill-GUIs samebackbone critic erring on 28 of 143 audited failures and passing at least four as successes [281]. Free-form goals and live websites lack scripts and fall to screenshot judges [101, 200, 201], which see the screen but not the backend state. Under optimization, ACuRL audits its judge against onpolicy trajectories over three rounds, with precision of 89.1% to 98.0% [15], whereas judge benchmarks score fixed trajectories [285] or the downstream success of policies trained on each judge [142]. Localization binds every source alike, even an exact checker spreading one verdict over episodes of up to 50 actions [281], with Lν falling as episodes lengthen. Loops recover step-level signal at credit-assignment cost through learned value functions and judges [14, 16, 135, 144] or failure-diagnosing critic for training-free revision [281], step-level advantages speeding DigiRLs learning by about 12% on its Web Shopping subset [14]. Localization Bought with Fidelity. With end states checkable, feedback acquisition falls short in localization and lacks checkers for free-form goals, and loops open the agent edge into FA to buy either. value function or reward model refit on the agents trajectories follows the policy, letting (k) move with each round and inviting compounding reward hacking, exploited errors re-entering the data on which it is refit [14, 135, 144]. MagicGUI-RMS slows this edge with GPT-4o reward model that arbitrates its domain model [144], yet both it and UI-Genie track their reward models only on fixed labeled sets, excluding the on-policy rollouts where exploitation would surface [135]. frozen self-judge keeps its bias fixed but shares it with the writer [162, 201, 278, 279, 281], its errors cutting revision short, as the over-optimistic EvoSkill-GUI critic shows. Verifiers fixed before the loop cut the edge, at the episode level in DART-GUI and MobileRL [17, 115] and at the step level in SEAgents World State Model [16], which localizes credit independently of the agent but exposes the loop to distribution shift once rollouts leave its training distribution. Localization and free-form goal coverage thus cost either fidelity that follows the agent or, from model fixed before the loop, distribution shift. ν

sections.title: 6.3 UC Bound by Generalization
sections.content: Update consolidation in GUI and Web navigation persists the scored experience in two forms, weight updates and trainingfree writes, each method using one of them  (Table 9)  . Weightupdating methods write Φθ with an update rule fixed before the loop, either continuously within single training run [14, 17, 115] or over two or three rounds through GRPO with adversarial imitation, reinforcement learning on generated 22 tasks, or fine-tuning of the agent and its reward model [15, 16, 135, 144], while SCALE fine-tunes its Selector and Predictor over repeated exploration rounds [284]. Trainingfree methods keep the backbone frozen and let the acting model write narrative, episodic, procedural, or grounding memory [278, 279, 282], tips and executable shortcuts [162, 280], or skill packages and executable APIs [201, 281], over one pass of task stream, few attempts per task, or fixed budget of practice iterations, whereas separate condenser writes the memory of WebCoach [163]. Retention and Generalization Constraints. Update consolidation is bound by generalization  (Table 5)  , documented within one platform and mostly on the task sets that produced the experience, whereas general capability, where measured, holds. No method measures retention on earlierround goals, and the closest evidence concerns general capability, ACuRL keeping or raising its scores on untrained environments by 2 to 7 points [15]. Elsewhere, replay sustains iteration robustness [14, 17], and per-round scores rise without reported reversal [135, 144, 284], though nonmonotonically in Mobile-Agent-E [162], tracking Jk on the current evaluation set, not Sζ . Training-free libraries evolve on their evaluation tasks [162, 163, 281], as in several fixed loops [104, 164, 187], measuring adaptation to known goal distribution. Held-out applications show transfer within the platform, MagicGUI-RMS gaining about as much on unseen apps as in domain [144], whereas ACuRL reaches new software version or operating system only by training there [15]. Zero-shot transfer across platforms appears only in the fixed loop GUI-HARVEST, whose frozen harness, evolved on OSWorld, adds 6.47 points for Qwen3-VL-32B-Instruct and 13.87 for GPT-5 on WindowsAgentArena [286]. Crossform comparisons are confounded by backbone, training-free loops mostly running frozen proprietary models and weightupdating loops open ones. Author Checks and Reader Dependence. What write carries into the agent is fixed in feedback acquisition, and the two forms of writing differ in what checks write before it persists and, for non-parametric writes, in who reads it afterward. Parametric writes pass on the verifiers score alone, carrying its exposure unchanged, compounding hacking for agent-derived verifiers [14, 135, 144, 284] and distribution shift for SEAgents frozen World State Model [16], while exact checkers leave little to inherit [17, 115]. Non-parametric writes pass an admission test that mostly reuses the authors judgment, EvoSkill-GUI and MobileSteward admitting skills and memories largely on their own critics verdicts [279, 281], whereas SkillWeaver unit-tests each synthesized API against execution feedback, check outside the writer [201]. Selfwritten skills can carry errors, such as the redundant or missing taps in the generated shortcuts of Mobile-Agent-E [162], unlike the keyor validation-gated writes of multimodal reasoning. Once admitted, non-parametric write takes effect only when later rollout reads it, its gain depending on the reader, as the memory that separate condenser writes for WebCoach lowers Qwen2.5-VL-7B from 32.8% to 31.1% yet raises Skywork-r1v3-38B from 47.3% to 61.4% [163]. nonparametric write is thus checked mostly by its author and valued by its reader.

sections.title: 6.4 Limits and Preconditions
sections.content: Bottleneck Attribution. In GUI and Web navigation, the quantity ceiling binds fixed and self-evolving loops alike, and self-reference leaves it in place, its cost lying in what each entry point puts at risk. Fixed loops pay the same episode cost, scaling to thousands of virtual machines in ComputerRL [269], and already train against signals fixed before the loop, the verification functions of ComputerRL at high fidelity and, below it, the screen judges of ZeroGUI [101] and MobileGUI-RL [130]. success-conditioned rule over task set with fixed checkers risks little, only the allocation following the agent [17], whereas generated goals move verification from fixed checkers to learned or prompted judges [15, 16, 201, 284], refit value functions and reward models buy localization with fidelity that moves with the policy [14, 135, 144], and frozen backbone that judges and writes carries one bias into both roles [278, 281]. The higher return of each scarce episode recovers part of these costs, controlled gains being reported for reuse, reweighting, and goal generation. No controlled comparison with fixed loops isolates these costs, which we read off the stage evidence and the provenance in Table 9. Cross-Cycle Degradation. Across cycles, self-reference opens paths along which degradation follows the agent, and the environment path adds shift specific to the scenario. On the goal side, success-conditioned rules and outcome-conditioned generators open the goal edge and agent-realized proposers extend the agent edge into σω [15, 16, 17, 115, 135, 201, 284], inviting curriculum collapse, which MobileRL risks by design in removing persistently failing tasks [17], and forgetting once the goal distribution moves, which replay mitigates [14, 17]. On the feedback side, refit verifiers extend the agent edge into FA, inviting compounding reward hacking untested beyond the two or three reported rounds, and training on self-generated trajectories invites model collapse [135, 144, 284], whereas frozen self-judges share fixed bias with the writer and open no such path. The extension into UC carries erroneous writes, which Mobile-Agent-E reports within single pass [162], and the environment path carries the drift of live websites between cycles, independently of the agent [200, 205]. Presupposed Resources. The mechanisms of GUI and Web navigation presuppose resources that its environments supply. Repeated attempts at goal, on which group sampling and reweighting rest, presuppose an environment that resets to known state [17, 115], checkers and screen judges presuppose an end state that program or model can inspect [16, 115], and non-parametric reuse presupposes reader able to exploit what the agent writes [163].

sections.title: 7 Self-Evolution in Embodied Manipulation
sections.content: Embodied manipulation occupies the quadrant of Figure 3 in which both ceilings are low on hardware, each rollout costing robot time, reset, and wear, and each outcome checkable only by per-task classifier or learned judge. Simulation relaxes both, where reinforcement learning against simulator success already forms fixed loops [62, 287, 288] and most self-evolving loops close before any hardware evaluation. The methods differ chiefly in feedback source: simulator 23 predicates keep fidelity, agent-derived verifiers densify feedback at the cost of an agent-tied bias, and external judges buy fidelity with per-query latency. Self-reference enters mostly through these verifiers in weight-updating loops and through memory, skills, and code that frozen model writes and judges in training-free loops. Reported loops run at most tens of rounds or bounded practice budget, and hardware evidence rests on eight to thirty evaluation trials per task.

sections.title:
7.1 EG Bound by Physical Rollouts
In embodied manipulation, experience generation draws
goals that pair a language instruction with a scene, and
each rollout is an episode of camera observations and robot
actions, emitted by a vision-language-action policy or by
programs that a language model writes over perception
and control primitives. The task families center on tabletop
and household manipulation in LIBERO and its variants,
ManiSkill, RoboCasa, RoboTwin, Robosuite, VIMA-Bench,
and VLABench [69, 190, 293, 294, 295, 300], extending
to memory-dependent tasks in RoboMemArena [292] and
physical tasks on robot arms [19, 21, 301, 305]. These goals
come from a benchmark suite, a library of scene-feasible tasks,
or the agent’s own proposals, and weight-updating loops run
groups of episodes in parallel simulators, training-free loops
sequential attempts, and hardware loops one episode at a
time, with RoboEvolve imagining episodes inside a learned
video simulator [298]. Table 10 summarizes the self-evolving
methods that satisfy the conditions of Sec. 2.3.
Quantity and Quality Constraints. Experience generation
is bound by both factors on hardware and chiefly by quality
in simulation (Table 3). On hardware, quantity binds through
physical time, human support, and scene recoverability,
each real-world experiment of Self-Improving EFMs running
about 20 hours with human station resets [19] and 6.58%
of the 456 autonomous episodes of Find Something You
Can’t Do ending in a scene that only a human restores [21].
Simulation lifts this bound with parallel environments and
group sampling [18, 62, 306], and where it also supplies a
success predicate, reinforcement learning needs no agent-
derived verifier and appears chiefly in fixed loops [95, 161,
287, 307, 308]. Quality binds on both sides, a long-horizon
task beyond the policy’s reach returning pg(1 − pg) ≈ 0, and
on hardware a persistent workspace leaves only part of a task
library feasible after each episode [21], each unreachable or
infeasible task costing a full physical rollout.
Task Choice and World Models. A larger group is
affordable only in simulation, which also supplies the success
predicate, and loops pull two other levers: task choice raises
E[IAk ] at a cost paid in verification, and a learned world
model buys rollouts at a cost paid in fidelity. Task choice
stays within a library or its edits, Find Something You Can’t
Do sampling scene-feasible tasks of low recent success [21]
and Reflection-VLA simplifying failing tasks through edited
simulation definitions [304]. Self-proposed practice extends
this choice [20, 166, 302] and needs a check for each new goal,
supplied by simulator predicates, by validation seeds that a
sealed judge grades in SEAR [20], or by verifiers of the agent’s
own model in RATs [302]. Controlled returns are reported
for both, removing the performance-aware curriculum of
Find Something You Can’t Do markedly slowing its real-
world improvement [21], failure-ranked collection lowering

sections.title: 7.2 FA Bound by Real-Robot Fidelity
sections.content: Each cycle hands feedback acquisition an episode of camera frames and actions, together with the simulator state in simulation, and Table 10 groups the methods by who supplies the feedback. Scores from the environment (e) come from simulator predicates, execution errors, and termination status [290, 292, 293, 294, 296, 297]. Scores from the agent (a) come from progress heads and value models frozen before reinforcement learning [19, 145, 299], from co-trained critic or reward proxy refit on the policys rollouts [25, 298], and from the frozen model that acts and then judges its own trials [20, 190, 300, 301, 302, 303]. Scores from outside the agent (b) come from VLM judges and critics [18, 21, 69, 304, 305]. Weight-updating methods turn scores into rewards or advantages for onor off-policy reinforcement learning [18, 19, 69, 145, 299], whereas training-free methods turn them into success labels and diagnoses that gate memory, skill, and code writes [290, 294, 300]. Fidelity and Localization Constraints. Feedback acquisition is bound on real robots by fidelity and by localization whose step-level signals inherit the fidelity of their estimators  (Table 4)  , the attainable fidelity being high in simulation and low on hardware. simulator predicate checks completion exactly, whereas on real robot judge must infer it from images with an accuracy reported between 69% and 100% across judges and test sets, from 100% for the best of five VLM judges on 100 image pairs in Find Something You Cant Do [21] to 78.9% for the judge of SOAR on 546 trajectories [173] and 69% to 75% for that of VideoAgent on 36 videos [172]. Cameras show an outcomes appearance and not contact or force, which judges reading images cannot observe. Under optimization, SEAR reports agents working around its sealed judge, for instance by reading object geometry from asset files [20], and policies trained against VLM judges learn to exploit them [143]. Localization comes only from learned estimators, such as progress heads, VLAC critics, and per-step verifiers, which return signal at every step or sub-goal [19, 69, 145, 302], whereas simulator predicate or real-robot judge returns one verdict per episode. Dense Feedback from Learned Verifiers. simulator predicate stays fixed as the policy improves, whereas the learned verifiers that make real-robot feedback dense or cheap incur degradations set by whether they follow the policy. Progress heads and value models frozen before reinforcement learning cut the agent edge [19, 145, 299] but meet distribution shift on states that the improving policy reaches outside its imitation data, the key challenge SelfImproving EFMs names for its reward model [19]. Co-trained critics keep the edge and invite compounding reward hacking, which RoboEvolve counters by binarizing its physical reward terms, citing as stability monotone reward curves that hacking would equally produce [298], and MERL by 25 down-weighting low-trust imagined chunks, outperforming matched control [25]. frozen self-judge opens no path into FA but writes its misjudged trials into the memory or skills it later retrieves [20, 190, 300, 301, 302], unless sealed judge checks them on validation seeds, judge that the agents of SEAR still circumvent [20]. External judges stay independent of the policy but cost 2.6 to 16.9 per query in Find Something You Cant Do [21], bounding the rollouts they can score. Dense feedback on hardware thus rests on fidelity audited within one task distribution, for judges on at most few hundred samples [21, 172, 173] and for the progress head on target-task demonstrations [19].

sections.title: 7.3 UC Bound by Generalization
sections.content: Update consolidation in embodied manipulation persists the scored experience in weight updates, training-free writes, or, in four methods, both  (Table 10)  . Weight-updating methods write Φθ with an update rule fixed before the loop, through reinforcement learning or fine-tuning on their own successes, RoboEvolve updating its video simulator alongside its planner [18, 19, 21, 25, 145, 296, 298, 299, 304]. Trainingfree methods keep the backbone frozen and let the agents language model write reflections [300, 301], skills, code, or harnesses [20, 190, 289, 290, 294, 297, 302, 303], or memory of verified behaviors and physical knowledge [291, 292, 293], over two to 50 rounds, rollout budget, or one pass of task stream. ViSkill [295], Agentic-VLA [69], and Robo-COP [305] train the policy alongside skill cards, memory of adapted weights, or admitted skills, and EmbodiedRSI keeps its VLA frozen while training the policy that manages its memory of code and skills [166]. Retention and Generalization Constraints. Update consolidation is bound by generalization  (Table 5)  , success falling with the distance of the test from practice even where gains persist within one benchmark, whereas retention is measured only in fixed loops, self-evolving ones guarding against regression by gates. The code policies of SEAR fall from 87.8% on new initial states of practiced tasks to 33.3% on new tasks and 28.7% under new simulator and action interface, and its trained VLAs from 73.2% to 43.1% and 10.2% [20]. Gains of written artifacts persist within one benchmark, SHAPER adding 2.5 points on its in-domain VLABench split and 6.0 to 10.0 on splits with unseen targets or task forms [190], although its absolute success on the splits with unseen targets falls from 42.5% to 26.0% and 19.5%. Hardware transfer is tested on small sets, five tasks of 30 trials each in EmbodiedRSI [166], eight scenes per task in RoboHarnEvo [291], and 20 tests per task in Robo-COP, which doubles success on only one of three held-out tasks [305]. Retention is measured only in the fixed loops CRL-VLA and Simple Recipe [95, 161] and approximated in self-evolving loops only by gates against regression, the adoption test of RoboCOP and the risk gate of Policy-Level RSI [296, 305]. As in navigation, backbones confound cross-form comparison: training-free loops mostly run frozen frontier models, weightupdating loops open ones. Tests outside the Writer. Feedback acquisition sets the exposure of consolidation, the two forms of writing differing in whether test outside the writer checks write before it persists. Parametric writes pass on the verifiers score, inheriting the distribution shift of frozen progress heads [19, 145, 299] and the compounding hacking of cotrained critics [25, 298], except where the adoption test of Robo-COP or the risk gate of Policy-Level RSI adds test outside the update rule [296, 305]. Non-parametric writes pass tests at different distances from the writer, from heldout seeds and fixed validation sets [190, 289, 297] through execution outcomes [290, 292, 293, 294] to the writers own judgment [20, 300, 301, 302]. write that only its writer checks persists with its errors, one SEAR run saving selfcalibrated placement verifier and finishing at 4.6% against 15.5% and 23.6% for two sibling runs without it [20]. test outside the writer matters even when it checks only task success, the harness of Scale and Selection falling from 40% to 0% over 20 rounds once every revision is accepted, whereas champion-challenger selection raises held-out success from 51% to 67% [297]. The farther the test sits from the writer, the more of the retained gain it protects.

sections.title: 7.4 Limits and Preconditions
sections.content: Bottleneck Attribution. In embodied manipulation, both ceilings bind fixed and self-evolving loops alike on hardware, self-reference changing who supplies the goal, the score, or the write but not the cost or attainable fidelity of physical rollout. Fixed loops meet the same ceilings, training against simulator success [62, 287] or letting separate model write memory or revise skill library [188, 309, 310, 311]. The cost of self-reference lies in what each entry point puts at risk: success-conditioned choice over fixed library risks little, only the allocation following the agent [21], whereas self-proposed practice moves verification to checks the agent builds [20], co-trained critic lets its bias follow the policy [25, 298], and frozen model that judges and writes carries one bias into both roles [300, 301]. Task choice and practice offset part of these costs, and only there are controlled gains reported [21, 302]. Beyond these ablations, the costs rest on stage evidence and the provenance in Table 10. Cross-Cycle Degradation. Across cycles, self-reference opens paths along which degradation follows the agent, and the environment path adds the sim-to-real gap. On the goal side, success-conditioned task choice, simplification, and failure-ranked collection open the goal edge [21, 296, 304] and self-proposed practice extends the agent edge into σω [20, 166, 298, 302], both inviting curriculum collapse. On the feedback side, co-trained critics extend the agent edge into FA, inviting compounding reward hacking [25, 298], and training planner on videos of its co-trained simulator invites model collapse [298], whereas frozen progress heads stay off the agent edge yet admit distribution shift [19]. The extension into UC carries erroneous writes [20] and regression when every checkpoint is deployed, below the frozen policy on three of the four tasks whose first candidate its gate rejected [305], while the environment path carries dynamics that loops closed in simulation never score. Within reported budgets, regression and erroneous writes are documented, whereas curriculum collapse, compounding reward hacking, model collapse, and distribution shift remain inferred. Presupposed Resources. The mechanisms of embodied manipulation presuppose resources that simulation supplies and hardware withholds. Reinforcement learning against success presupposes simulator success predicates [62], heldout gates simulated or deployment trials [289, 305], learned hardware feedback an audited judge [21, 173], and written artifacts test outside the writer [20, 297].

sections.title: 8 Cross-Scenario Asymmetry
sections.content: This section characterizes the cross-scenario asymmetry, in which the two directions of scenario pair receive different kinds of portability verdict, mechanism that applies in one scenario needing an adaptation, being blocked, or becoming redundant in the other while the reverse direction meets different combination. We interpret the asymmetry through two properties of each scenario, which factors are scarce there, exogenously or through resources that self-reference gives up, and which task-structural resources and conditions it holds, chiefly output equivalence, checkable outcomes, and outcome observability. mechanism is portable on target that holds the resource it presupposes, conditional where that resource is held only on sub-family or after an adaptation, blocked where the outcome it judges or must check is unobservable, and redundant where the factor it raises is not scarce. The account concerns the kind of verdict each direction receives and leaves aside cost differences across scenarios, which the generation-verification gap would set. Quadrant placements and cost comparisons are inferred from single-scenario evidence, and the verdicts remain untested.

sections.title: 8.2 Task-Structural Resources
sections.content: Whether meta-operator that the agent realizes can raise scarce factor varies across scenarios only with resources that the scenario holds independently of the agent. We call task structure the part of scenario fixed before any choice of agent or meta-operator, namely the environment family and evaluation distribution of the macro-environment (Definition 4) without its goal sampler, together with the interfaces through which loop resets, replicates, or inspects its environments, property being task-structural when replacing the agent and its three meta-operators leaves it unchanged. Task-structural resources decide whether mechanism that presupposes them is defined or affordable, whereas capabilities of the agents model and artifacts authored before the loop, the two other kinds mechanism can presuppose, hold on every target. Resources by Scenario. Three task-structural resources recur across the scenarios and are held unequally, output equivalence, checkable outcomes, and resettable rollouts. Output equivalence, held by short discrete answers but not by images or action trajectories, defines majority voting without converting outputs into answers. Checkable outcomes give each newly posed or reweighted goal its own reference outside the agent, coming from keys, generation programs, state scripts, or screen judges [14, 64, 115, 152, 316, 317, 318, 319]. Resettable, parallelizable rollouts let group sampling scale, at the price of emulator and virtual-machine instances where episodes run in software environments [14, 125]. Reasoning holds all three, navigation checkable outcomes and bought rollouts, generation free rollouts with checks only on program-checkable sub-families [191, 195], and manipulation checks and bought rollouts only in simulation [62], hardware episodes costing physical time [19, 21]. The verdicts turn chiefly on output equivalence and checkable outcomes, rollouts entering them only through K, which decides whether world models are redundant. The ceilings of Figure 3 reflect these resources only in part, navigation keeping low under per-step latency despite resettable rollouts and sharing high with reasoning, which alone holds output equivalence. Portability is therefore derived from the resources of each scenario, not read off its quadrant. Observability and Online Checks. Two further conditions decide whether held resource serves the loop, the observability of the outcome, which task structure fixes, and an online check built on the resource, which the loops design supplies or omits. The outcome is observable where it appears in the agents observations or in check available to the loop, condition that every mechanism judging or checking it presupposes. An online check, check built on resource that runs inside the loop, is the only route by which the resource lowers the realized cost of trade-off, and loops run one wherever answer keys, execution results, 27 or simulator outcomes are available, training-free methods checking their writes against them [146, 201, 290]. Holding resource does not ensure such check, task streams, open prompts, and self-chosen practice tasks leaving none even in navigation, as in WebCoachs task stream [163]. The frozen acting model then judges its own episodes and writes the update, as in ManimAgent [256], Mobile-Agent-E [162], and SEAR [20], and an error of judgment enters the update unchecked, one simulated SEAR run saving self-built verifier wrong on 91% of later rollouts. loop without an online check thus gives up resource that its scenario holds.

The goal sampler supplies the agents success record or its own proposals in place of fixed goal distribution, the feedback function the agents judgment in place of an answer key or checker, and the evolution operator the agents authorship in place of an update rule written in advance. Each trade-off pays what the supplied output lacks relative to the replaced component and presupposes resource that is task-structural, capability of the agents model, or an artifact authored before the loop. Of its three elements, the factor raised, the resource presupposed, and the price paid, only the first two enter the portability verdicts. Experience Generation. The mechanisms of experience generation raise E[IAk ], scarce in every scenario, and differ in what they give up to raise it, with learned world model as the one exception. Success-conditioned allocation reweights fixed task set, giving up coverage of the tasks it down-weights and presupposing checkable outcomes on that set. Created goals, posed by the agent or generated from its record, extend the factor beyond fixed pool but give up the answer key or checking script of each pooled goal, presupposing in its place an outcome that something other than their generator can check or answers that vote can compare. 8.4 Costs and Alternative Sources
The evidence on the price paid, the trade-off element the
verdicts leave out, serves the account in two ways, setting the
cost of the conditional routes the verdicts open and bearing
on whether a factor other than scarcity and resources could
produce the asymmetry. The comparisons below each stay
sections.content: inside one paper, bearing on mechanisms gain and, where measured, its cost. Degradation, the rest of the cost, is left aside, its evidence too uneven for cross-scenario comparison. Generation-Verification Gap. The generation-verification gap prices trade-off wherever the agents own judgment serves as the reference, as capability that holds on every target (Sec. 8.3), and remains inferred in multimodal loops. Introduced for language models, the gap is the improvement model obtains by filtering or reweighting its own generations with its own verification [322]. We extend the term by separating task-level component, the difference in difficulty between verifying and generating on task family, from model-level component, the difference between the verification and generation accuracy of the agents own model on the same goals. The model-level component remains unestimated, multimodal audits reporting only the verification side [64, 256, 281], and backbone priors would confound it even once measured (Sec. 3.5). We infer the tasklevel component to be large in GUI and Web navigation, where final screen can be inspected without replaying the steps that reach it, and small in open-prompt generation, where judging whether an image satisfies prompt calls on the compositional understanding that producing it requires, difference that makes the cost of self-judgment vary across scenarios even where its verdict does not. Evaluator Fidelity. The feedback ablations order evaluators by fidelity and thereby price the conditional routes that substitute judge for missing check. Two ablations, both in generation, compare verifier built on the agents own judgment with the evaluator it replaces, frozen self-rater against program check in one and co-trained reward model against learned preference scorer in the other. In RSI in UMMs, training on the better of two images as rated by the frozen starting model gains 0.5 points, against 8.6 points with execution-verified charts for the same requests and steps [191]. The reward model that The Image as Its Own Reward [245] co-trains against reference images matches the PickScore of Flow-GRPO [195] trained on PickScore and wins 70.0% of the authors human image-quality comparisons against it, model that the same raters place below its base. verifier built on the agents own judgment thus falls below program check and can exceed learned preference scorer, an ordering whose two ends come from different verifiers, one frozen and one co-trained, and which the other scenarios leave untested. The ordering would be contradicted if such verifier outperformed keyed or programmatic check at matched budget on fixed goals. Goal-Mechanism Gains. Goal mechanisms gain in all four scenarios with one reported exception, consistent with scarcity of E[IAk ] that gives this factor no part in the asymmetry. Removing allocation hurts both scenarios that ablate it, MobileRL [17] losing 6.3 points of AndroidWorld success without its failure curriculum filter and Policy-Level RSI [296] raising its ManiSkill failure rate from 2.34% to 3.36% under random scene selection. Created goals lead untrained, random, or frozen-source generators in VisPlay [5], RATs [302], ACuRL [15], and RSIgen [260], and trail the NNetNav curriculum by 1.3 points in one SEAgent setting [16]. Within program-checkable family the error-driven chart distribution of RSI in UMMs leads fixed distribution with the same number of verified charts by 2.8 to 4.1 points in every round [191]. These comparisons come from the authors of each method and may overstate the gain, yet their agreement across the four scenarios leaves the verdicts on goal mechanisms to turn on the resources they presuppose. Writer Dependence. The gain of reuse depends on the writer, model-level dependence that travels with the agent to every target and adds no asymmetry of its own. Authored writes outperform skill-free or raw alternatives in two navigation ablations, EvoSkill-GUI [281] gaining 6.7 points on MobileWorld over pass@3 without skills and Agent [278] 7.7 points on an OSWorld subset over full trajectories in place of its self-evaluators summaries. SEAR [20], holding the scenario fixed and varying only the writer, finds the sign of this gain reversed, GPT-5.6-sol on RoboLab dropping from 46.9% without library to 42.4% with its own, beyond the spread of three runs, and rising to 60.6% with one that Claude Opus 5 wrote, loss the authors trace to objectlocation recipes with few grasp checks. Whether such content tracks the generation-verification gap of the writers model is untested, and library that gained the same whoever wrote it would contradict the dependence on the writer.
